findings.title: Kept verdicts carry no version of the rule that made them, so a fix to what counts as the wallet's never reaches rows and boxes an older release already judged
findings.scenario:
Mainnet with the private index on (the default). A payment to the user's Seedelf register whose inline datum is constructor 0 written as tag 102 with an indefinite pair, 102([_ 0, [g, u]]), which the node decodes as the contract's Register (r3a#1's verifier). chain.ts registerOf refuses it, so 1.9.1's readIndexView judges the row not ours: dropped at a snapshot, or sealed as checked[ref] = false above the cursor and dropped once the cursor passes it. Then a release ships whose registerOf accepts that spelling (the fix for r3a#1's class). After the update it reads the same sealed record (v === 1) and checks only rows it hasn't checked before. On every device that already saw the row, the money stays out of the private balance for good: at the contract, spendable only by this key, never shown. That lasts until Remove wallet and a restore (a snapshot), a rollback under the cursor, or Koios-only, whose session cache re-reads in full.

The other direction: x2#2's planted row (a key address whose hash is the contract's), if the index lists it, is sealed into `rows` as ours. x2#2's fix, in ownedUtxos or as a data-layer filter, never removes it: settled rows aren't checked again, and nobody can ever spend that UTxO, so it never leaves through `gone`. The balance keeps counting it and Max keeps failing.

The same family:
- Lovejoin's sealed `origins` are asked of only where missing, so e1a#1's fix doesn't reach a stranger's deposit box already looked up while it stays listed.
- Discovery's Koios height resets only when the token list changes, and that list is byte-identical at every tag since 1.6.0. 1.7.x advanced the height past v2 launches its verify_pool refused (chunk 44a: 'Wallets already installed drop v2 pools'). So a Koios-only mainnet device updated from 1.7.x to 1.8.0 could never find mainnet's v2 5 ₳ pool (block 14167059) by a look, until 1.8.1's head start bundled it.
- The copies read once (`checked`) are never read again, so r3a#1's fix doesn't reach a restored wallet's box in a copy that a stranger's mix rewrote before that one read.

Nothing is stale today: registerOf (2026-09-27), ownedUtxos (e69697b4, in 1.4.0), is_owned and madeBy haven't changed since these records began.
findings.since: 1.4.0 (b5ad15a7) for the sealed contract view; Lovejoin origins before 1.0.0 (independent review M14); the pools' height and copies-read 1.6.0 (1772c96f)
findings.evidence:
contract-scan.ts:264 `let settled = kept?.v === 1 && kept.owner === owner ? kept : undefined;` (the only gate that forces a snapshot, besides a missing or unreadable record, a rollback, or a refused cursor at :267-272).

contract-scan.ts:281 `rows: snapshot.rows.filter((r) => mine.has(r.ref)).map(settledRow)`: rows judged not ours are never kept.

contract-scan.ts:294-297: `const unchecked = changes.created.filter((r) => !(r.ref in settled.checked)); ... for (const r of unchecked) checked[r.ref] = fresh.has(r.ref);`

contract-scan.ts:301 `const atTip = [...settled.rows, ...changes.created.filter((r) => checked[r.ref])].filter((r) => !gone.has(r.ref));`: settled rows are not re-checked.

contract-scan.ts:315 folds in only `checked[r.ref]` true.

ballances.ts:489-506 ownedUtxos = registerOf + keys.seedelf.isOwned. Its own comment at :497-498: 'which the private index's sealed record would keep for good'.

chain.ts:92-97: `if (tag.arg === CONSTR_ANY) { const pair = headAt(b, at); if (!pair || pair.major !== 4 || pair.arg !== 2) return undefined; ...`, which refuses an indefinite pair.

lovejoin.ts:7926-7932: read() keeps any origin with a boolean `mixed` and a number `seen`.
lovejoin.ts:6140 `const unknown = owned.filter((b) => !known(b) && !kept[b.txHash]);`
lovejoin.ts:6187 `.filter((tx) => !said[tx])`
lovejoin.ts:1976-1979 knownOf includes origins.
sortOut 6068-6070 refreshes `seen` while the box is listed.

lovejoin-pools.ts:388 `const height = stored?.listed === listed ? Math.max(head.height, stored.height) : head.height;`
lovejoin-pools.ts:570 advances the height to the highest holder row, whatever was refused at :583-587.
lovejoin-pools.ts:327-331 and :338-351: copies in `checked` are never read again.

Tags (git show of src/tokens/list.json and src/lovejoin-pools.json at web-wallet/1.6.0 through 1.9.1): list.json sha256 prefix 1a96804077c47618 at every tag. Mainnet head start: 1.8.0 height 14139313 with only dc6abe3b0b (8131b1d); 1.8.1 height 14167059 with fcb3f5ec5f (v2).

git log -L on registerOf and ownedUtxos: last changes aad95b12 (2026-09-27) and e69697b4 (in 1.4.0). seedelf-crypto register.rs is unchanged since 1.4.0.
findings.fix:
Tie every kept verdict to the rule that made it, and make it again when the rule changes. Fix the class, in four places:
- contract-scan.ts: bump `Settled.v` (264 already turns a mismatch into one snapshot, the same request every wallet makes) in the release that changes registerOf, ownedUtxos or is_owned.
- lovejoin.ts origins: keep each origin's input credentials, sealed, and derive mixed/public/account at read time (this also mends gap-g6#2); or drop origins written under an older rule version.
- lovejoin-pools.ts: fold the recognised script sets into listFingerprint, so an update that recognises a new set looks again from the head start.
- Clear the copies-read `checked` set when the box reader changes.

For chunk 51: the fixes for x2#2, r3a#1's class (if extended to chain.ts) and e1a#1 should carry their record's invalidation.

Test, in the style of private-index.test.ts:87: seal a Settled record holding a row today's ownedUtxos refuses, plus `checked: { [ref]: false }` for a row it accepts. readIndexView returns the first as owned and never the second.

findings.title: After a restore, what made a box is kept with only the accounts then known, so a custom account's (index 24 or more) deposit boxes read as the private balance's for good
findings.scenario:
The user adds public account 30 by its number and Bootstraps (or mixes, stopped before every box was mixed) from it into the v2 5 ₳ pool. Later they restore the phrase in another browser, or Remove wallet and restore. The restore's discovery finds sequential accounts only, so 30 isn't known when the first pool read looks up what made the boxes:
- accountKeys derives the active account, the known ones and 0-23;
- madeBy finds no account for the deposit's input;
- the origin is sealed as { mixed: false } with no `public`.

The user then adds account 30, but the origin is never asked of again. From then on those boxes are 'not mixed yet' and no account's:
- Mix my boxes again from the private balance (publicToo off) takes them first, mixing account 30's deposit boxes in a privately funded session. On chain that ties account 30 to the session and its private funding, which privacy.md:454 says it doesn't do ('takes only the others').
- A box brought back records no tie in its history (depositAccountOf), so a later private spend that merges it says it ties nothing new, though its way back ties account 30 on chain (PRIV-3).

With account 1 the refusal works (lovejoin-accounts.test.ts:190). Past 23, nothing reaches it.
findings.since: 1.2.0 (4279db80, accountKeys' index set); the history ties since 1.6.0 (PRIV-3)
findings.evidence:
lovejoin.ts:6323-6324: `const known = (await this.deps.knownAccounts?.().catch(() => [])) ?? []; const indexes = [...new Set([active, ...known, ...Array.from({ length: MAX_PROBE }, (_, i) => i)])];` (MAX_PROBE = 24, accounts.ts:46).

lovejoin.ts:6251-6259: `whose` finds the account by payment key among those alone; `told.set(tx_hash, { mixed: ..., ...(account !== undefined ? { public: true, ... } : {}) })`. lookUp seals it (6198-6199) and never asks again (6187 `!said[tx]`; found 6140 `!kept[b.txHash]`).

lovejoin.ts:2122-2127 originOf reads `told?.public`. 2237 `fromPublic` filters on it. fanOut 3788 `const left = new Set(again && !publicToo ? [...fromPublic(split.owned, schedule), ...untold].map(ref) : [])`. 3819-3820 put not-mixed-yet boxes (depositsOf, 2000-2007) first.

lovejoin.ts:2276-2277 `return told?.public && mixedFor(told, poolOf(b)) === false ? (told.account ?? 0) : undefined;`: no tie, so withdrawOne's `ties` and tiedOrigin (2286) are empty.

accounts.ts:260-273: discover stops at the first unused sequential account; a custom index is reached only by add/check (privacy.md:189).

lovejoin-accounts.test.ts:190-210 pins the account-1 case only.
findings.fix:
Keep the inputs' payment and stake credentials in the sealed origin (as the private index's provenance or tx_info gave them), and derive `public`/`account` at read time from the accounts known then. Alternatively, when accounts.ts adds an account (add, check, discover), re-derive the origins that name none. Asking Koios again would repeat M14's accepted cost; deriving from kept inputs asks nobody. This is gap-g6#1's fix for origins.

Test: lovejoin-accounts.test.ts:190 with account 30 in place of 1. It shows origins[D] without `public` and againBoxes not refusing. Then `t.accounts.add(30)`, and againBoxes should refuse as it does for account 1.

guards.stops: read() normalises each field of a sealed schedule an older release wrote (due, counts, marks, leaves, origins, depositors, asking, pools, launches, copies, mixes, bringing, counted, bringStopped, retired): a stray shape is left out rather than crash a run or be taken for data
a 1.5.0 record with no list of mixes gets its entries made from its chains before any change, so no mix's boxes go uncounted or a Bootstrap unheld
a chain cut before the `cut` flag existed (English words) is still read as cut, so its maybe-sent step is settled as cut rather than stopped
retireOnce: a 1.7 record's Bootstraps, counts and tails in retired pools are let go, ended or dropped once, and the retired pools' run is asked, so 1.7 boxes don't wait for mixes that never come
a pool a record names that the read set lacks leaves retireOnce undecided, never retiring v2 pools on a read that fell back (R3)
a 1.7 tile Mix or Mix again session with no pool is the classic pool's: its chain is refused there (retired) and the session comes back directly, saying why, never into a retired pool

pricedClassic: a swap approved before 1.8.0 (no auto.lovejoin.box) comes back in no more 5 ₳ boxes than its 10 ₳ approval priced, never twice the mixes and fees it showed (critic#4, with lovejoin.ts:3744-3747)
acrossOf drops retired token pools, so a 1.7 approval naming an 8131b1d token pool brings that token back directly (poolCant) rather than into a retired pool
guards.test: none found pinning the 1.7 approval itself (lovejoin-retired.test.ts covers retired pools)

guards.stops: a 1.7 collateral tail in a retired 5 ₳ pool is marked over and never built there; the session's rest comes back

STATE-4: a device's Koios height holds only under the token list it was read under, so an update that lists more tokens looks again from the head start (not under a change of recognised script sets: gap-g6#1)
a history class written as bare 'public' before several accounts reads as account 0's, so selection doesn't split one account's money in two or say false ties
a sealed record that won't open (another phrase's, damaged, a newer format) throws UnreadableRecordError, never reads as empty and gets written over
a maybe-sent withdraw kept across a wipe (update, closed browser) has its inputs held as spent again before it's looked for, so no other build takes its box meanwhile
guards.test: tests/lovejoin-bring-all-back.test.ts:487 (looks for a withdraw Koios didn't answer; not checked for this line)

guards.stops: a maybe-sent withdraw is dropped SPENT_KEEP_MS after it was first kept, so a stale one (refused at every resend) never holds every other way back for good
a vault of an unknown version is refused in words rather than opened as SBV1
every preference an older release kept is validated with its default (e.g. dappPassword on, lovejoinCollateral on), so a missing or bad value never weakens a protection
sorted() keeps only valid public indexes (never the one-time account 24301'), so an old record can't make a session's account a public one
a sealed contract view of another wallet or another version is never taken for this one's: a snapshot is read instead (the gate a rule-version bump would use, gap-g6#1)
Remove wallet deletes every local key any release since 1.0.0 wrote (vault, unlock failures, preferences, sealed records but the kept two, pool, governance, price and Lovejoin-pool caches)

checked_ok: The update premise: chrome.storage.session is wiped at an extension update (sw.ts:62, 1.7.0's x-upgrade lens), so only chrome.storage.local crosses versions. I diffed every local record's type at each tag from web-wallet/1.6.0 to 1.9.1 against today's readers.

lovejoin.<net>: the only shape changes since 1.6.0 are additive and all from 1.8.0 (Schedule.retired, Bringing.retired, bringStopped.retired, LaunchRecord.version). ChainRecord's and Withdrawing's required fields are the same at 1.0.0, 1.2.0, 1.3.0, 1.4.0, 1.5.0 and HEAD, so read() keeping `chains` and `withdrawing` unvalidated is safe for every release's records.

sessions.<net>: only auto.lovejoin.box was added (1.8.0); its absence means classic pricing (critic#4). SessionRecord and AutoRecord are stable since 1.0.0. The nested types (SessionTx, SessionPause, RetryReason, UnsentWhy, SwapQuote, LeftBehindUtxo, LovejoinFunding, LovejoinChainTx, DappSite, Contact, KnownAccount, PendingTx) are identical in rpc.ts at 1.6.0 and HEAD; enums only grew (LovejoinUnusable 'retired').

Old sessions on today's code: a 1.7 tile Mix or Mix again session (no mix.pool) is refused in the classic pool and comes back directly. A 1.7 swap whose approval names an 8131b1d token pool brings that token back directly. A 1.5.0 swap (no width or tokens) goes three wide with its tokens back directly (wayOf 6417-6418).

Old Lovejoin state on today's code: a 1.7 tail in an 8131b1d 5 ₳ pool is ended. A 1.7 Bring every box back run is widened, kept or asked afresh. 1.7 Bootstraps in retired pools are released. retireOnce is byte-identical in 1.8.0 and 1.9.1, so a 1.7-to-1.9.1 jump runs the transition 1.8.0's live update (G1) exercised.

A 1.5.0-to-1.9.1 jump still meets 1.6.0's migrations: entries made from chains, wasCut's English words, Origin.account absent read as account 0, and the legacy 'public' history class. lovejoin-1-5-0.test.ts:946/966 carry a 1.5.0 vault through the retirement.
maybeSent.<net>: pending.ts is unchanged since 1.6.0, so the sealed watch is read by the code that wrote it. sessions.ts stillWatched (2605-2624) reads only fields every Watched has.
lovejoinMaybe.<net>: KeptMaybe is unchanged. keptUnsettled, publicMaybe and adoptKept read it as written, and adoptKept deletes another phrase's.
Vault: secret-box is unchanged since chunk 5 (db18375c). It uses fixed SBV1 parameters, the magic names the scheme, and VaultRecord stays version 1.
Preferences: every field is validated with a default on read, and set writes the whole normalised object, so an old or partial record never weakens dappPassword, lovejoinCollateral or the like.
accounts, contacts, coins, dapps, history, mintedBy and contract.mainnet: their modules are unchanged since 1.6.0. PRIVATE_RECORDS only grew (accounts in 1.2.0, contract.mainnet in 1.4.0).

Every chrome.storage.local key written at 1.0.0, 1.2.0, 1.3.0, 1.4.0, 1.5.0, 1.6.0 and 1.9.1 is either in reset's removal list (vault, unlockFailures, preferences, private.*, pools.*, govActions.*, prices, lovejoinPools.*) or kept on purpose (network, account, language, openIn): no orphan survives Remove wallet.
seedelf.lovejoinPools.<net>: a FoundPool with no `version` reads as 8131b1d's, which every pool kept before 1.8.0 is; valuesOf keys copies per set; the earlierCode migration (R2-4) still runs.

1.8.0 to 1.8.1 and 1.8.1 to 1.9.x changed only session-storage shapes (KeptBack and KeptPublic `balances`, Reservation `takes`), which an update wipes. A missing `balances` means no reward read, which at worst is a refusal, never money.

The content scripts are registered under fixed names (cip30-page.js, cip30-bridge.js), so a registration Chrome keeps across an update points to files the new package has; onInstalled re-applies the connector.
After an update the wallet is locked (its entropy is in session storage); the unlock re-arms the sessions and auto-lock alarms, and the unlock's run sends nothing.
No release ever allowed the one-time account 24301' as a public account: the refusal (631c5b02) shipped in 1.2.0, the release that brought several accounts.
notes: Assumption: chrome.storage.session is cleared on an extension update. This comes from Chrome's storage documentation, the code's own premise (sw.ts:62, pending.ts:34-39) and 1.7.0's x-upgrade report; I didn't test it here. If Chrome ever kept it, the session-only shapes that changed since 1.6.0 still read safely: an absent `balances` or `takes` means no reward read, giving a refusal, never money.

src/tokens/list.json is byte-identical at every tag from 1.6.0 to 1.9.1 (sha256 prefix 1a96804077c47618), and the bundled `listed` fingerprints are the same too. So STATE-4's height reset never fired on any update since 1.6.0, and the v2 change of 1.8.0 was saved only by head starts. 1.8.0's mainnet head start (height 14139313) lacked mainnet's v2 5 ₳ pool (fcb3f5ec5f, block 14167059); 1.8.1's has it. That is the past instance behind gap-g6#1's pools member.

New fact on settled backlog worker#3 (a way back resent for two hours, refused as IncompleteWithdrawals). It has a version-skew cause too: a 1.8.0 Withdrawing (zero withdrawal, built before chunk 43) that was maybe-sent at the update to 1.8.1, once a reward balance appears at that pool, is resent and refused until SPENT_KEEP_MS from `at`. Every other way back waits meanwhile (settleWithdrawing returns true). The wait is bounded, and no money moves.

For the fix round (gap-g6#1): the fixes for x2#2, for r3a#1's class if chain.ts registerOf learns the indefinite pair, for e1a#1, and for gap-g1#1/#2 change rules whose verdicts are kept on the device. Each needs its record invalidated (bump Settled.v; re-derive or drop origins), or it reaches only rows and boxes seen after the update. History classes are derived at read time (activity.ts classOf 646-670), so a reclassification there reaches old entries; one made in `arrived` (427-470) doesn't.

chain.ts registerOf (92-97) takes tag 102 only with a definite pair, so a payment to the user's register written as 102([_ 0, [g, u]]) is invisible to the private balance on both read paths today. This is the critic's weak claim about E6/X3; I found no filed finding for the contract reader itself, only x3#1 (the sign window) and r3a#1 (Lovejoin boxes).

Harmless oddities: empty() (lovejoin.ts:2328) omits `retired`, `unlock`, `marks` and the top-level `unsure`. update() writes whenever a record exists, and unsure is a subset of notMixed. PrivateStore.get never checks `Sealed.v`: only v1 exists, so a future seal format needs a branch there.

Re-reading after a rule change costs little in privacy. A Settled snapshot is the same request every wallet makes. Discovery's height and copies-read are unsealed and the same for every device with the same history, so a holder look from the head start is neutral. Re-asking Koios what made boxes would repeat M14's accepted cost; keeping each origin's input credentials avoids it, and also mends gap-g6#2.

gap-g6#2 is a same-release knowledge gap, not version skew, but it sits in this lane's files and in the same family of kept verdicts never made again. Its impact matches e1a#1's (verified medium); I graded it low for its preconditions (a custom account of index 24 or more, plus a restore), and the impact verifier may weigh it higher.
